acquisition_note: Retrospective source inspection; original information cutoff and selected market snapshots unchanged. Date-only publication is not assigned an invented intraday clock.

minutes.fact: July 28–29 meeting: many participants saw tightening as likely necessary if inflation failed to fall; some doubted financial conditions were restrictive enough.
minutes.revision: July meeting discussion published August 19; not an August 19 policy decision.

july_statement.fact: 3.50–3.75% target maintained; three dissenters preferred a 25 bp increase. Known before the August 19 minutes.

buybacks.fact: Maximum per-operation liquidity-support buybacks of 10–20y and 20–30y nominal bonds increase from USD 2bn to at least USD 4bn, effective September 9 through November 4.
buybacks.revision: Announcement about future operations; not same-day purchases or a Federal Reserve QE announcement.

morning_gold.fact: Body describes a morning gold rally after the Treasury announcement, while minutes were still due at 18:00 GMT. Exact Treasury announcement time remains unverified.
morning_gold.expectation_limit: Analyst description of surprise was after the announcement; not an archived pre-announcement consensus. Article spot/futures prices are not used in this report's contract statistics.

warsh_preview.fact: Investors sought clarity on the inflation response and whether higher bond yields reduced the need for policy hikes; few expected explicit forward guidance. Some considered bond-market tightening sufficient.
warsh_preview.expectation_limit: Diverse investor views, not a survey consensus. The article's intraday 40% rate-hike quote is not substituted for the selected August 27 FedWatch date record.

warsh_speech.fact: Warsh did not describe broad financial conditions as restrictive; confidence that underlying inflation was moving clearly and sufficiently fast toward target was needed. No specific meeting action was promised.
warsh_speech.revision: Speech, not a policy decision or revised statistical release.

weekend_risk.fact: US strikes on Iranian targets reported August 30.
weekend_risk.revision: Exact occurrence, first-publication and update times unverified; no precise event-time marker.

monday_gold.fact: Reporting linked gold weakness to continuing post-Warsh hike expectations and renewed oil/inflation concerns after weekend conflict. It also noted a modest dollar pullback.
monday_gold.revision: Use the updated version only by its update time, not by the earlier publication time. Not ex-ante evidence.

cme_calendar.fact: Sunday September 6 pre-open orders are for Tuesday September 8 trade date; Tuesday has normal Globex close. September 7 is excluded as a separate regular trade date, not treated as a missing observed close.

cme_settlement.fact: Normal September 4 settlements; no September 7 COMEX settlements. This does not mean no holiday intraday trading.

calendar.close_convention: Exact 17:00 America/New_York bar end; source bar starts 16:55; not an exchange settlement.

pre_expectation.limit: Prior hawkish dissent known; no verified pre-release minutes surprise measure or Treasury buyback forecast.

cases.actual_revision: No new policy rate set; minutes describe July. Treasury enlarged future operations.

cases.label: 8/28：Warsh讲话

pre_expectation.limit: Qualitative investor expectations plus prior-date FedWatch, not a quantified speech consensus.

cases.actual_revision: No statistical prior-value revision or new rate decision.
other_news_in_forward_window: September 4 employment and prior revisions (E5) enter +5.

cases.label: 8/31：周末风险后的首个日终

pre_expectation.limit: No ex-ante forecast of the weekend strike; Friday pricing already incorporates Warsh.

cases.actual_revision: Rolling news without a fully timestamped first-release archive.
other_news_in_forward_window: Continuing post-Warsh monetary repricing overlaps throughout.
September 4 employment and prior revisions (E5) enter +4.
September 7 is not a separate regular COMEX trade date; +5 is September 8.

known_limits: No complete intraday cross-market rate/dollar/oil/position data to establish the full transmission order.
Sunday August 30 first available gold bar ends 18:15 NY; first two five-minute bars absent. Never label it the opening price.
Same-day driver comparisons use each source's date; they are not synchronized-close or first-release measurements.
Cases and horizons are selected retrospectively; multi-day returns include other news and are not isolated causal effects.
